subject: Reef AI trial runway — evaluation criteria, capacity ask, and rollout timeline
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@reef.ai>; ops@reef.ai
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 7 May 2027 15:23:00 -0400
Subject: Follow-up: trial runway & capacity asks (post-demo)

Thanks again for taking the demo today — great alignment on what success looks like. I wanted to capture the agreed evaluation scope, a proposed capacity plan for the 30-day trial, and clear owners/next steps so we can get provisioning scheduled.

Quick recap of customer goals (from the call)
- Primary: Replace current on-prem transformer scoring service for customer-facing recommendations — need consistent 99th-percentile latency < 350ms at peak traffic.
- Secondary: Validate quality parity vs. current model (BLEU/qualitative) for a 10k-sample prompt set.
- Risk/constraint: Data residency in US-east and no PII leak to other tenants.

Suggested trial evaluation plan (what to measure)
- Perf: p50/p95/p99 latency for 128/512 token requests, sustained throughput (reqs/sec) at target concurrency, cold-start duration with KV cache warm-up.
- Quality: end-to-end scoring on your 10k prompt set; regressions flagged via the shared spreadsheet.
- Reliability: error-rate < 0.5% under synthetic spike tests; graceful fallback to smaller model if capacity constrained.

Capacity ask (initial proposal)
- Reserved baseline: 2 x A100-80GB equivalent slots for the duration of the POC (30 days). This supports steady-state traffic and gives headroom for parallel evals.
- Autoscale policy: allow autoscale up to 6 nodes for burst windows (30–45 minute bursts) driven by queue length; scale-down cooldown 10m.
- Burst expectation: tolerate short bursts up to 4x baseline for up to 45 minutes during scheduled load tests.

Owners & next steps
- Liam / Reef ops: confirm target traffic profile and share the 10k prompt set (action: ops@reef.ai) — due Tue 2027-05-11.
- Aditya (infra): validate reserved slot availability and cost implication; estimate lead time to reserve by 2027-05-12.
- Marissa (CS): produce the evaluation sheet and pass/fail thresholds (I attached a template).
- Jasmine (me): schedule kickoff & test calendar once capacity is reserved.

Attachments: reef_eval_template.xlsx (simple pass/fail metrics + sampling instructions), network_diagram.png (example VPC peering layout).

If everyone agrees, I will trigger the capacity reservation request Monday and send a calendar for the 30-day window.

- Jasmine
Jasmine Liu
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
https://redwood.com
From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@reef.ai>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@reef.ai
Date: Sat, 8 May 2027 09:18:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Follow-up: trial runway & capacity asks (post-demo)

Thanks Jasmine — that matches how we heard it. A couple clarifications from our side:
- The 10k prompt set will include both short (<=64 tokens) and long (up to 800 tokens) queries; we expect a minority (~15%) of long requests which can increase memory pressure.
- Peak concurrency target for our UAT traffic is roughly 40 concurrent active sessions, translating to ~55 reqs/sec for the expected prompt mix.
- Security: we need an audit log of all inference requests and the option to disable caching for certain datasets.

For success criteria, we propose:
- Latency: p95 <= 350ms for mixed-length workload at 55 reqs/sec
- Quality: no more than 3% regression on the provided BLEU-based metric across the sample set
- Ops: ability to rotate KMS keys and export audit logs daily

We accept the 2 reserved nodes baseline, but can you confirm the instance type (A100-80GB or equivalent) and if the autoscale can be limited to the same-region capacity? Also please confirm any minimum billing commitments for reserved slots.

I'll drop the sample prompt set in the Drive link tonight and ops@reef.ai will follow up on the audit-logging question.

- Liam
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@reef.ai>; Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 8 May 2027 12:05:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Follow-up: trial runway & capacity asks (post-demo)

On Sat, 08 May 2027 at 09:18, Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@reef.ai> wrote:
> We accept the 2 reserved nodes baseline... can you confirm the instance type... and if the autoscale can be limited to the same-region capacity?

Liam — thanks for the details. Short answers: yes, we can reserve 2 A100-80GB-equivalent inference slots in us-east-1 as your baseline. Autoscale can be restricted to same-region capacity; we will not burst cross-region unless you explicitly opt-in.

Sizing rationale & proposed config:
- Baseline: 2 reserved nodes (A100-80GB or equivalent) configured with continuous batching and prefix KV cache. This covers the 55 reqs/sec mixed workload with p95 headroom for short requests.
- Burst: allow autoscale up to 6 total nodes in us-east-1. We'll configure a short 2-minute warm-up policy for new nodes and prioritize cold-start-sensitive routes on cached paths.
- Caching: default enabled for performance; we will add a per-request header toggle so you can opt certain prompts out (meets audit requirement).
- Audit logs: we can stream inference request metadata to your S3 bucket daily (no payloads unless you opt-in).

Operational notes:
- Reservation lead time: we can provision the reserved baseline within 48 hours of signed SOW or exec approval.
- Billing: reserved trial slots are billed at the trial rate outlined in the trial SOW; no long-term commitment if you don't convert.

Next steps I will take this week:
- Open the reservation order for 2 baseline nodes in us-east-1 and flag the autoscale cap to 6 (action: Aditya) — ETA 2027-05-10 EOD to confirm provisioning window.
- Share a small runbook for launch & load tests.

If that works, Jasmine please confirm kickoff timing and Marissa will own the evaluation metrics collection.

— Aditya
Senior Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@reef.ai>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@reef.ai, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 9 May 2027 11:12:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Follow-up: trial runway & capacity asks (post-demo)

Perfect — thank you both. Ops will upload the prompt set to the Drive link tomorrow and confirm S3 details for audit logs. We agree to the baseline 2 A100-80GB slots + autoscale to 6 in us-east-1. Please proceed with provisioning and send a tentative kickoff window (we prefer 2027-05-13 to 2027-06-11).

I'll also add a short list of GRC questions in the Drive doc — Marissa, feel free to ping me if you need clarifications on the pass/fail criteria.

See you on the kickoff.

- Liam
